messages.subject: issue defining sliding semilandmarks
parts:
Hello all,
I have been trying to define some sliding semilandmarks on a 3D specimen (ply format) using geomorph.
I have successfully imported the ply file and defined 4 landmarks (see matrix below), but when I try to tell geomorph that I want 2 of those landmarks
to be sliding semilandmarks I get an error message:

 xpts       ypts       zpts
1  8.651276 -26.862196 -19.222791
2 13.844276 -21.862196  -7.222791
3 17.259276 -14.862196   6.777209
4 14.887276  -6.687196  17.777209

> define.sliders(Acro, nsliders=2, surfsliders=FALSE)

Error in CV[i, ] <- landmarks[1:3] :
  incorrect number of subscripts on matrix


What am I doing wrong? Any help would be greatly appreaciated!

Alessandro

messages.author: 91722721526eb1d7
messages.subject: Re: issue defining sliding semilandmarks
parts:
Hi Alessandro,

Interesting. First of all, i'd expect there to be an error appear when you have surfsliders=FALSE rather than null, actually as below:

library(geomorph)
Loading required package: rgl
Loading required package: ape
> data("scallops")
> define.sliders(scallops$coorddata[,,1], nsliders=2, surfsliders=FALSE)
Error in file(file, "rt") : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning message:
In file(file, "rt") :
  cannot open file 'surfslide.csv': No such file or directory

In any case, when I use the first specimen of the scallop dataset and run just using 4 landmarks I get this:
> define.sliders(scallops$coorddata[1:4,,1], nsliders=2, surfsliders=NULL)
semi-landmark 3 slides between landmarks 2 and 4 
semi-landmark 2 slides between landmarks 3 and 1 
     before slide after
[1,]      2     3     4
[2,]      3     2     1

Things work fine. So the issue isn't with 4 landmarks and defining 2 semis which is what I suspect. Instead I and wondering what you are putting in as the object "Acro". This should be a p-x-k matrix of x,y,z coordinate data for the landmarks.

The alternative is that you can simply write your sliders matrix as follows:

> define.sliders(c(1:4),2)
     before slide after
[1,]      1     2     3
[2,]      2     3     4

This uses the AUTO mode of the function, to create a sliders matrix based on four landmarks, the middle two of which slide between those end points.

Emma
